I farm the same way I have for many years. Last year my wheat did alright, and maize was a little better because rain came at the right time. I do what most people in our village do — no need to change what works.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed from the dealer in town — everyone uses this kind now, the old seeds give too little. Before planting I spread diammonium phosphate, about 2 bags for my land (one bag is 50 jin, so about 50 kg each), and some urea mixed in. Then at green-up in spring I top-dress with urea, maybe 1 bag and a half. I water the wheat 3 times — before winter, at green-up, and at heading. Wheat here cannot grow without irrigation, our wells are reliable. I plough before planting because the stubble from maize needs to go down. I spray against aphids and weeds, usually 2 times. Last year I got about 500 jin per mu (250 kg), but when I calculate in kg I think more like 480 kg per mu in a good year.

For maize, after wheat harvest in June I plant right away, no-till with the seeder, saves time and diesel. I use hybrid seed — everyone does, the yield is much better than the old kind. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, then top-dress urea when the maize is knee-high. Maize here gets most water from summer rain, but if July is dry I water once from the well. I spray for corn borer and armyworm when I see them, 2 times usually. My maize gives about 1200 jin per mu (600 kg) when the weather is good.

My daughter-in-law helps at planting and harvest, and my son sends money from the city for fertilizer. I don't want to spend too much, but I also don't want a bad harvest — better to put a little extra fertilizer than to lose yield. That is how I think about it.
